standard_prerequisites.name: Tutte-Berge formula
standard_prerequisites.statement: The matching deficiency equals max over U of odd(G minus U) minus |U|.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Source237-243, citing Berge1962; the exact formula is printed as allowed context.
standard_prerequisites.use: Translate bounds on odd components, and the explicit constructed obstruction, into matching existence/nonexistence.

standard_prerequisites.name: Classical Cartesian-product edge-connectivity formula
standard_prerequisites.statement: For connected regular factors of sizes M_i and total degree d, lambda(product)=min(d,min_i lambda(H_i) product_(j!=i) M_j).
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Source318-335, citing Hammack, Imrich and Klavzar, Handbook of Product Graphs (2011), Chapter5.
standard_prerequisites.use: This exact classical structural formula is explicitly permitted; its proof is not part of the counted task.

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary finite counting and real inequalities
standard_prerequisites.use: Parity of a cut, exponential-versus-linear estimates, and the number/order of Cartesian-product components.

core_obligations: Convert edge-connectivity >=d-1 into Tutte-Berge control using parity of every odd-component boundary, then show the product reaches this threshold.
Build the regular m-branch obstruction H and amplify by triangles while preserving odd components so 3^(t-1)<m violates Tutte.

proof_roadmap.step: Odd component boundary has parity d, so a d-1 cut lower bound gives d; sum its edges into U and apply Tutte-Berge.
Lift a factor matching if possible; otherwise all factors have order at least3, and product edge-connectivity grows exponentially with dimension.
Build the m-regular hub graph on (m+1)^2 vertices from m copies of the odd-order gadget. Its product with t-1 triangles has m odd components after removing only 3^(t-1) hub vertices.
